title: Fresh Bay low-pressure area may ease AP’s rain woes - The Times of India
full_text:
Visakhapatnam: A fresh low-pressure area has formed over the north Bay of Bengal and neighborhood, and the system is to trigger moderate to heavy rainfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh for the next two days. The farmers of north Andhra Pradesh are eagerly waiting for a good spell of rain to sustain the kharif crops.
The IMD forecasts parts of the NTR, Krishna, Eluru, West Godavari, East Godavari, Kakinada, Konaseema, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalle, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Srikakulam districts on Friday (Sep 11).
Motorists wade through a waterlogged road after a sudden downpour in Vijayawada on Thursday. Pic: SS Vijay Babu
On Saturday, parts of the Anakapalle, Kakinada, East Godavari, West Godavari, Konaseema, Eluru, NTR, Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts are likely to witness heavy rainfall. Parts of the Vizag city and neighbouring Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Srikakulam and Parvathipuram Manyam districts recorded rainfall on Thursday.
Five to six low-pressure systems have formed over Bay of Bengal in 2026, but Andhra Pradesh has received little rain, V Ganesh, a resident of MVP Colony in Vizag, said. He hoped the latest system would bring rainfall to the city and surrounding districts.
With over 46 per cent of rainfall deficit and depletion of groundwater source, Vizagites are experiencing water crisis this year. Residents in parts of the city are struggling to meet their daily water requirements.
The state’s rainfall deficit, measured from June 1, stood at 45% at the end of August, and increased to 47% on Sept 10. The state recorded 218.7 mm of rainfall against the seasonal normal of 412.6 from June 1 to Sept 10.
All 28 districts in the state are currently rainfall-deficient, with 26 districts categorised under ‘deficit’ and two districts-Annamayya and Prakasam suffering under ‘severe deficit’ (60 per cent deficit) condition. The deficit rainfall in Rayalaseema as well as coastal AP has raised concerns over kharif agriculture, reservoir storage, ground water table and drinking-water availability.
The weathermen said parts of Andhra Pradesh have been recording extreme weather conditions (hot and humid weather conditions, dry spells and heatwave like conditions) for the past two months due to strengthening El Nino. On Sept 9 (Wednesday), heat wave conditions prevailed at Kakinada and Narsapur in the state. The strengthening of the El Nino disrupted the southwest monsoon.
